description:
🚀 Building AeroFlame-X: An interactive microgravity combustion dashboard powered by NASA PSI datasets (FLEX, BASS, Saffire, ACME) for ISS and Artemis lunar habitats (30% O2).

As a UBIT Software Engineering student, I’ve deployed a live app tackling spaceflight fire safety and am looking for passionate collaborators (devs, designers, or data buffs) to join forces. Let's win Global!
summary:
The Problem
Traditional buoyancy-driven fire safety mechanisms fail in microgravity, where flames form spherical diffusion droplets and invisible "cool flames" continue low-temperature oxidation without triggering standard detectors. These critical smoke detection lags and risks are magnified exponentially in oxygen-enriched Artemis lunar habitat atmospheres (30% O2).

The Solution (AeroFlame-X)
AeroFlame-X is an advanced, interactive web-based microgravity fire hazard dashboard and telemetry simulator. Grounded in rigorous NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion datasets—including FLEX, BASS, Saffire, and ACME—our platform bridges historical orbital research with an intuitive operational tool to protect astronaut crews.

Key Features & Impact
The dashboard features real-time cabin pressure and temperature modeling, a live simulation of ISS versus Artemis habitat environments, and dynamic airflow trade-off calculations that pinpoint the optimal balanced ventilation setpoint (~23 cm/s) to minimize fire spread while accelerating smoke detection. Complete with automated PDF safety reporting, AeroFlame-X provides mission operators with actionable, real-time hazard intelligence.
details:
What does it do and how does it work? In deep-space habitats, a single undetected spark can turn catastrophic within seconds. AeroFlame-X is a mission-critical, interactive web-based microgravity fire hazard dashboard and telemetry simulator built to stop that threat before it starts. It models complex combustion, pressure, and thermal dynamics in space—directly contrasting standard International Space Station (ISS) baselines with volatile, oxygen-enriched Artemis lunar habitat atmospheres (30% O2). Grounded in millions of data points from NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) research archives (FLEX, BASS, Saffire, and ACME), our simulator calculates dynamic airflow trade-offs in real time, locking in the precise optimal ventilation setpoint (~23 cm/s) needed to suppress fire spread while slashing smoke detector response times.

What benefits and intended impact does it have? In microgravity, normal buoyancy-driven fire safety completely breaks down: flames form erratic spherical diffusion fronts, and invisible "cool flames" sustain hazardous low-temperature oxidation up to ~700 K without triggering traditional alarms. AeroFlame-X equips mission operators and habitat engineers with an operational early-warning telemetry shield against these invisible killers. Its ultimate impact is safeguarding future Artemis lunar crews, preventing catastrophic habitat fires, and instantly generating automated, audit-ready PDF safety reports.

What tools, coding languages, software, or hardware did you use?

  • Frontend & Backend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (Node.js, Express) powering a high-performance interactive web interface and real-time telemetry calculation engine.
  • Deployment & Version Control: Vercel (for instant, high-speed cloud deployment) and GitHub (for robust source code architecture).
  • Data Sources & Research: Millions of records from NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion datasets (FLEX, BASS, Saffire, ACME).
  • Design & Documentation: Canva and automated PDF generation tools for professional structural architecture and reporting.

How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider? AeroFlame-X transforms millions of raw, complex aerospace fluid dynamics data points into an intuitive, high-stakes tactical dashboard. Our team engineered this by solving a brutal physical paradox: increasing cabin airflow accelerates smoke detection, but too much velocity fans hidden, oxygen-rich flames. By mathematically identifying the exact ~23 cm/s "sweet spot" ventilation threshold, AeroFlame-X bridges heavy theoretical orbital physics with lightning-fast, life-saving operational design.
